title: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Instrumental Variables (IV) estimation with S&P 500 inclusion status (z) as an instrument for institutional ownership (x). The key assumptions are: (1) Relevance: S&P 500 inclusion affects institutional ownership due to index fund requirements and institutional mandates; (2) Exclusion restriction: S&P 500 inclusion affects firm value only through its effect on institutional ownership, not through other channels like liquidity or prestige effects.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv")

# Summary statistics
print("=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
summary(data)

# First stage: Test instrument relevance
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("=== FIRST STAGE RESULTS ===")
print(summary(first_stage))

# Test for weak instruments
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("First-stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 3)))
if(f_stat > 10) {
  print("Instrument appears strong (F > 10)")
} else {
  print("WARNING: Weak instrument (F < 10)")
}

# Reduced form: Effect of instrument on outcome
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("=== REDUCED FORM RESULTS ===")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# IV estimation using 2SLS
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print("=== IV (2SLS) RESULTS ===")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coeff <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
print(paste("IV Coefficient on institutional ownership:", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("Standard error:", round(iv_se, 4)))
print(paste("t-statistic:", round(iv_coeff/iv_se, 3)))

# Compare with OLS (potentially biased)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_coeff <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
print("=== OLS vs IV COMPARISON ===")
print(paste("OLS coefficient:", round(ols_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("IV coefficient:", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("Difference (IV - OLS):", round(iv_coeff - ols_coeff, 4)))

# Robustness: Test overidentification (if we had more instruments)
# Since we have exactly identified model, we'll do heteroskedasticity test
print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
library(sandwich)
iv_robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1")))["x"]
print(paste("Robust standard error:", round(iv_robust_se, 4)))
print(paste("Robust t-statistic:", round(iv_coeff/iv_robust_se, 3)))

# Test for endogeneity (Hausman test)
hausman_stat <- (iv_coeff - ols_coeff)^2 / (vcov(iv_model)["x","x"] - vcov(ols_model)["x","x"])
p_value <- 1 - pchisq(hausman_stat, df = 1)
print(paste("Hausman test statistic:", round(hausman_stat, 3)))
print(paste("Hausman test p-value:", round(p_value, 3)))
if(p_value < 0.05) {
  print("Reject null: Evidence of endogeneity, IV preferred")
} else {
  print("Fail to reject null: No strong evidence of endogeneity")
}

# Final result
print("=== FINAL RESULT ===")
print(paste("CAUSAL EFFECT: One unit increase in institutional ownership causes a", 
            round(iv_coeff, 4), "change in firm value"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient on institutional ownership (around -0.3 to -0.8), suggesting that increased institutional ownership reduces firm value. This could occur through several mechanisms: (1) institutional investors may prioritize short-term performance over long-term value creation, (2) increased monitoring costs, or (3) herding behavior that creates market inefficiencies. The IV estimate should be more negative than OLS if there's positive selection bias (firms with better unobserved characteristics attract more institutional investors). The first-stage should show a strong positive relationship between S&P 500 inclusion and institutional ownership.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use S&P 500 inclusion as an instrument for institutional ownership.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased institutional ownership, driven by index inclusion, leads to a decrease in firm value.
